findings.who: A married couple filing jointly. The spouse was a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico and excluded Puerto Rico wages. They have no child under 17 with an SSN, so line 4 is zero, but they claim a 19-year-old student as an other dependent on line 6.
findings.why_no: No filer answer is involved. The gate is computed from line 4 = 0, so the Puerto Rico residency question is never asked and puerto_rico_if_child is false. That is correct for line 16b and Credit Limit Worksheet B line 2. The risk is the gated line's claim that 'the Puerto Rico path changes no amount'. If line 2a, or a prompt for it, is derived from this flag, the excluded Puerto Rico income drops out of modified AGI.
findings.line: s8812.puerto_rico_if_child (only if it also drives line 2a, which sets the line 3 phaseout income for the credit for other dependents)
findings.irs_text: f1040s8812 (2025) p. 1, line 2a: "Enter income from Puerto Rico that you excluded"; Part I applies whenever line 6 > 0, regardless of line 4.
findings.fix: Ask line 2a, or a Puerto Rico residency question that feeds it, whenever line 4 + line 6 > 0. Do not derive it from puerto_rico_if_child. Restrict this gated line's description to line 16b, Part II-B and Credit Limit Worksheet B.

locators: p. 3, Bona Fide Residents of Puerto Rico, "If you were a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico, you may be eligible to claim the ACTC if you had at least one qualifying child"
